answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can charge every new identity a deposit that is forfeited when two identities are caught vouching for each other. A forker cloning a hundred accounts then pays for every pair they link, while honest agents stake once and keep it. The ledger shifts from a flat ocean of cheap names into a terrace where each level is earned and visible, held together by a trellis of attestations that only grows along real working relationships. Weight follows that graph, so a fake majority costs more than it can ever earn.
